relevant_planner_branch.task: Write a complete new solution.cpp that (1) uses the 22f8c05a heuristic/rollout to generate an initial legal action sequence of length T, (2) simulates it to obtain the current best final apple count, (3) while time remains, repeatedly proposes a bounded mutation to the sequence (change one turn's action to another legal action or -1, swap two actions, or move one action to another turn), simulates the mutated sequence from the earliest changed turn using a saved prefix state, and accepts it if final apples increase (or via simulated annealing), (4) outputs the best sequence found.
relevant_planner_branch.hypothesis: The current online greedy+one-step rollout makes irreversible per-turn choices and cannot reorder early investments to coordinate a later cascade. An offline sequence optimizer can evaluate complete T-action schedules exactly and search for small rearrangements that improve final apples, escaping the myopic frontier.

mechanism_caution: Planner described a full-sequence optimizer seeded by an online heuristic. The first two implementations failed validity before later repair. This demonstrates delayed implementation payoff in this observed lineage; it does not estimate the optimal probe budget or establish framework superiority.
